prev: Date: November 14, 2007
next: I. Purpose This policy is intended to protect employees from the hazards associated with the unexpected release of energy during the setup, maintenance or servicing of machines or equipment and to maintain compliance with 29 CFR 1910.147. II. Scope This policy applies to all City of Westminster (City) employees performing maintenance or servicing operations on any equipment or machine in which the unexpected startup or release of stored energy could cause injury to an employee. This procedure contains general fundamental requirements essential for compliance and nothing in this procedure shall be construed to prohibit individual departments from exceeding the requirements established in this policy/procedure. In such cases, Departmental Standard Operating Procedures should be coordinated with the Risk Coordinator, Office of Human Resources. III. Responsibility

text: IV. Definitions
next: A. Affected employee - an employee who works in an area where servicing or maintenance operations are performed under lockout/tagout. B. Authorized employee - an employee who performs service or maintenance on machines and implements lockout/tagout procedures in order to guarantee his/her protection. An affected employee becomes an authorized employee when that employee’s duties include performing servicing or maintenance operations. C. Energy-isolating device - any mechanical device that physically prevents the transmission or release of energy. D. Energy source - Any source of electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, hydraulic, chemical, thermal, or other energy. E. Lockout - the placement of a lockout device(lock) used to secure an energy isolating device in a safe position that prevents the unexpected operation of equipment or machinery until its removal.

text: V. Preparing for Zero Energy State (ZES)
prev: H.
next: A. Any employee who is assigned a duty that involves the installation, repair, removal or maintenance of equipment shall determine if the uncontrolled release of energy could occur, and if so, that lockout/tagout procedures are followed. B. Employees to be affected shall be notified by the individual(s) performing the maintenance. C. All sources capable of uncontrolled or stored energy release shall be identified and controlled. D. All personnel shall be cleared from any potential exposure to uncontrolled release of energy until ZES is achieved.

next: VI. Implementing ZES

text: VI. Implementing ZES
prev: D.
next: A. The affected equipment or machinery shall be turned off or shut down using normal operating procedure. B. All energy isolating devices shall be locked out and tagged out by an authorized employee(s). C. All other energy sources shall have a lockout device applied to achieve ZES. D. All stored energy sources shall be released or controlled. E. Before beginning maintenance or servicing, attempt to activate the machinery using normal operating controls to assure ZES. F. Energy sources having the potential for re-accumulation of energy to a hazardous level shall be checked during the maintenance operation to assure that ZES is maintained. G. When more than one authorized employee is working on the same machine, each employee shall place his/her lockout device and tag on each energy isolating device for added security (crew lockout).

next: VII. Return to Operating Condition

text: VII.
prev: VII. Return to Operating Condition
next: A. All authorized and affected employees shall be notified of the intent to return the equipment or machine to operating condition. B. The authorized employee shall inspect the equipment or machine to assure tools and service equipment have been removed. C. The machine or equipment shall be inspected by the authorized employee to ensure that components are operationally intact. D. All guards or similar safety devices shall be replaced and inspected or adjusted as needed. E. All controls and operating devices shall be verified to be in the “off” position and the machinery rendered inoperable. F. All employees shall be removed from the machinery to a safe area. G. All authorized employees shall remove their lock and/or tag from the energy isolating device(s). H. A final visual check shall be performed by the authorized employee to assure that no individuals are exposed to any hazards of the equipment or machinery. I. The machinery shall then be re-energized.

next: VIII. Lockout/Tagout Devices

text: VIII. Lockout/Tagout Devices
prev: I.
next: A. Lockout/Tagout devices shall be provided to authorized employees by their department. B. The authorized employee shall utilize a tag with every lockout device and indicate his/her identity on every tag used. C. Lockout devices shall be substantial enough to prevent removal without the use of substantial force, such as the use bolt cutters. D. Tagout devices shall be substantial enough to prevent inadvertent or accidental removal. The tags shall have a minimum unlocking strength of 50 pounds. E. Lockout/Tagout devices shall be utilized for the specific purpose of Lockout/Tagout. These devices may not be utilized for any other purpose. F. Lockout/tagout devices shall only be removed by the authorized employee who installed the device.

next: XI. Training A. Employees shall receive instruction on this procedure and its application consistent with their assigned duties. B. Retraining shall be provided for employees when their job duties change; a change in machines, equipment or processes that present a new hazard; a change in the energy control procedures; or whenever the employer believes that there are deviations from or inadequacies in the employee’s knowledge or use of the energy control procedures. XII. Program Evaluation A. Supervisors, employees, and the Risk Coordinator shall evaluate this program at least annually to ensure program effectiveness and identify any deviations or inadequacies within the program 1. The evaluation shall be performed by an authorized employee other than the ones(s) utilizing the energy control procedure being evaluated. B. Evaluations shall be documented through a certification. The certification shall identify the machine or equipment on which the energy control procedure was being utilized, the date of the evaluation, the employees included in the evaluation, and the person performing the evaluation.
